name: ssd-bench-structured-regex-gen
notes: Structured: regex generation with detailed spec and test cases. ~600 prompt tokens. Output is regex patterns + explanations.

messages.content:
Generate a set of production-quality regular expressions for the following use cases. For each regex, provide: (1) the pattern itself, (2) the flags required (case-insensitive, multiline, etc.), (3) a brief explanation of each group or construct, and (4) at least three positive test cases and two negative test cases.

Use Case 1 — Semantic Version String (semver.org spec):
Match strings of the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional pre-release and build metadata. Examples that must match: 1.0.0, 2.3.14, 1.0.0-alpha.1, 1.0.0-beta.2+build.123, 0.0.1-rc.3+exp.sha.5114f85. Examples that must NOT match: 1.0, v1.0.0 (leading v), 1.0.0., 1.0.0-+build (empty pre-release before +).

Use Case 2 — ISO 8601 UTC Timestamp:
Match timestamps of the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fff]Z or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z (fractional seconds optional, 1–6 digits). The date and time components must be individually valid: months 01–12, days 01–31, hours 00–23, minutes 00–59, seconds 00–59. The regex need not validate February's maximum day count. Must match: 2026-05-14T03:47:00Z, 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, 2026-12-31T23:59:59.999999Z. Must NOT match: 2026-13-01T00:00:00Z, 2026-05-14T25:00:00Z, 2026-05-14T03:47:00 (no Z suffix), 2026-5-1T0:0:0Z (non-padded fields).

Use Case 3 — SQLite WAL Journal File Path:
Match file paths for SQLite WAL and SHM journal files. The base database file has a .db extension. The WAL file is the base path with -wal appended; the SHM file with -shm appended. Match paths that are either the base .db, the -wal, or the -shm variant. The path may contain forward slashes and hyphens in directory and file components. Examples that must match: /tmp/rmlx.62265.claim/index.db, /home/user/.rmlx/metrics/runs.db-wal, /var/data/my-project_cache/index.db-shm. Must NOT match: /data/file.json, /data/runs.dbwal (missing hyphen), /data/index.db- (trailing hyphen without suffix).

Use Case 4 — OpenAI-Compatible Model ID:
Match model IDs of the form NAMESPACE__MODEL-NAME-VARIANT where NAMESPACE is lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (no leading/trailing hyphens), MODEL-NAME-VARIANT contains lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and dots. The double underscore __ is the separator. Examples that must match: mlx-community__gemma-4-e2b-it-mxfp8, z-lab__qwen3.6-27b-paro, prism-ml__ternary-bonsai-8b-mlx-2bit. Must NOT match: mlx_community__gemma (underscore in namespace), mlxcommunity-gemma (missing double-underscore separator), mlx-community__ (empty model name), --bad__model (leading hyphen in namespace).

Use Case 5 — IPv4 CIDR Block:
Match IPv4 CIDR notation: four octets 0–255 separated by dots, followed by / and a prefix length 0–32. Each octet must not have leading zeros (0 is valid; 00, 01 are not). Examples that must match: 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.0/24, 0.0.0.0/0, 255.255.255.255/32. Must NOT match: 10.0.0.256/24, 192.168.01.0/24, 10.0.0.0/33, 10.0.0.0, 10.0.0.0/ (missing prefix length).
